title: 4 weeks out. Legs B in the books. 📚
hook: 4 weeks out. Legs B in the books. 📚
caption:
4 weeks out. Legs B in the books. 📚

Dropping 12kg from my peak gaining phase means the weights definitely feel heavier right now but it is all part of the process.
This is where strategy comes in. The key to minimizing strength loss during a deep cut is keeping calories as high as possible for as long as possible, while smartly managing your training volume.

Full Legs B ⬇️
1. Adductors x2
2. BB RDLs x2
3. Pendulum Squat x2
4. Horizontal Leg Press x2
5. Leg Ext x3
6. Lying Leg Curls x2
7. Smith Split Squats x2
8. Cybex Eagle Calve Raises x3

hook: My body. Also my body, 12 hours later.
caption:
My body. Also my body, 12 hours later.
Not a “before/after,” not a fail, just what real bodies actually do.
Bloat happens, water retention happens, your gut moves food and gas through it at different rates depending on what you ate, your hormones, your stress, how much you slept. None of that is you “losing progress.” It’s you being a human being with organs.

hook: Rest isn’t something you have to earn. It’s part of the work.
caption:
Rest isn’t something you have to earn. It’s part of the work.

Your body doesn’t get stronger while you’re constantly pushing—it gets stronger when you give it time to recover, rebuild, and come back ready for more.

More workouts. More cardio. More steps. More restriction. More hustle.
More isn’t always better.

Sometimes the most productive thing you can do for your goals is sleep, eat enough, slow down, and recover.

Because rest doesn’t interrupt your progress.
Rest supports it.

Recover without guilt.
